name: Atmos
description: Protects against destructive Atmos operations like terraform deploy \ (auto-approve), destroy, clean, state rm/taint, and helmfile destroy

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-plan-destroy
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform plan -destroy previews destruction. Review carefully before deploying.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform plan -destroy shows a destruction preview:

\ - Read-only (safe to run), but shows what WOULD be destroyed \ - Review the output carefully before applying/deploying

\ This is the safe way to preview a destroy.

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-destroy
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform destroy removes ALL managed infrastructure for the component/stack.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform destroy removes managed infrastructure:

\ - Every resource in the component's state is destroyed \ - --affected / --all destroy across MANY components at once \ - Cannot be undone without backups/recreation

\ Preview first: atmos terraform plan -destroy <component> -s <stack>

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-deploy
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform deploy runs apply with -auto-approve (no confirmation). Preview with 'atmos terraform plan' first.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform deploy auto-approves an apply:

\ - Atmos rewrites 'deploy' to 'apply' and injects -auto-approve \ - Changes are applied immediately, with no confirmation prompt \ - May destroy or recreate resources

\ Preview first: atmos terraform plan <component> -s <stack>

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-apply-auto-approve
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform apply -auto-approve skips confirmation. Remove -auto-approve for safety.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform apply -auto-approve skips confirmation:

\ - No opportunity to review the plan before applying \ - Intended for CI/CD, not interactive use \ - Changes may destroy or recreate resources

\ For safety: drop -auto-approve and review the plan

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-clean
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform clean deletes local Terraform state and generated files (.terraform/, varfiles, backend config; --everything also removes terraform.tfstate*).
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform clean removes local Terraform working files:

\ - Deletes .terraform/, generated varfiles, and backend config \ - --everything also removes local state (terraform.tfstate*) \ - --force skips the confirmation prompt \ - Back up any local-only state before running

\ Inspect what would be removed before using --everything --force

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-taint
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform taint marks a resource to be destroyed and recreated on next apply.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform taint marks a resource for recreation:

\ - The resource is destroyed and recreated on next apply/deploy \ - May cause downtime; identifiers/IPs may change

\ Prefer -replace in plan/apply (Terraform 0.15.2+)

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-state-rm
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform state rm removes a resource from state without destroying it. Resource becomes unmanaged.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform state rm orphans a resource:

\ - Removed from Terraform state, but the cloud resource remains \ - The resource becomes unmanaged (Terraform ignores it) \ - May cause drift between state and reality

\ Back up state first (atmos terraform state pull)

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-state-mv
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform state mv moves resources in state. Incorrect moves can cause resource recreation.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform state mv rewrites resource addresses:

\ - A wrong move can cause destruction/recreation \ - Does not affect the actual cloud resources

\ Preview the move and back up state first

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-force-unlock
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform force-unlock removes a state lock. Only use if the lock is stale.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform force-unlock removes a state lock:

\ - May corrupt state if another operation is in progress \ - Only use when you are sure no other run is active

\ Verify no other operations: CI/CD pipelines, other operators

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-workspace-delete
destructive_patterns.description: atmos terraform workspace delete removes a workspace and its state.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos terraform workspace delete removes a workspace:

\ - The workspace and its state file are deleted \ - Does NOT destroy actual infrastructure (resources orphaned)

\ Destroy resources first, then delete the workspace

destructive_patterns.name: atmos-helmfile-destroy
destructive_patterns.description: atmos helmfile destroy removes Helm releases from the cluster.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
atmos helmfile destroy tears down Helm releases:

\ - Deletes the component's Helm releases from the cluster \ - Workloads, services, and their data may be removed \ - Cannot be undone without redeploying

\ Inspect first: atmos helmfile diff <component> -s <stack>
